title: 醉花阴（薄雾浓云愁永昼）
author: 李清照
intro: The Double Ninth Festival, and her husband is far away. A young wife spends a long grey day alone, drinks among the chrysanthemums at dusk — and ends with one of the most famous lines in Chinese: “I am thinner than the yellow flowers.”
analysis: 这是李清照年轻时写的词，丈夫赵明诚出门在外，正赶上重阳节。上阕写白天和夜里：雾薄云浓，白天长得让人发愁，香炉里的香慢慢烧完；本该团聚的节日，她一个人躺在纱帐里，半夜凉意透进来。下阕写黄昏：她学陶渊明在“东篱”下赏菊饮酒，衣袖里沾满菊花的清香，却没人可以分享。最后三句是全词的高潮：别说这样不让人伤心——西风卷起帘子，帘里的人比外面的菊花还要瘦。“瘦”字一语双关：菊花在秋风里细瘦，人因为思念也消瘦了。用花比人，含蓄又生动。相传赵明诚读后不服，闭门写了五十首词，把这首混在里面请朋友看，朋友说只有这三句最好。
analysisEn: Li Qingzhao wrote this as a young wife, when her husband Zhao Mingcheng was away from home on the Double Ninth Festival (重阳, the ninth day of the ninth lunar month), a day for being with family, climbing hills and enjoying chrysanthemums. The first half is the day and the night: thin mist, heavy clouds, a day that drags on; incense slowly burning down in a bronze burner shaped like a beast. Then night, alone on a jade pillow behind gauze curtains, and the first chill of autumn seeping in. The second half is dusk. She drinks by the “eastern hedge” — a nod to the poet Tao Yuanming, who picked chrysanthemums there — and the flowers’ scent fills her sleeves. But there is no one to share it with. The ending is the famous part: don’t say this doesn’t break the heart — when the west wind lifts the curtain, the woman inside is thinner than the yellow flowers. 瘦 (“thin”) works both ways: the chrysanthemums are slender in the autumn wind, and she has grown thin from missing him. A traditional story says her husband, a little jealous, wrote fifty lyrics of his own and slipped hers among them; a friend read them all and picked out just these last three lines.
background: Li Qingzhao (1084–c. 1155) is China’s most celebrated woman poet. This lyric is traditionally dated to the early years of her marriage, when her husband was serving away from home; she is said to have sent it to him.
pronunciation: 薄雾 bó（文读；口语也可读 báo）；重阳 chóng；帘卷 juǎn；瑞脑 ruì nǎo（龙脑香）。
version: 采用通行文本。异文：“浓云”一作“浓雰”；“金兽”一作“香兽”；“佳节”一作“时节”；“玉枕”一作“宝枕”；“凉初透”一作“秋初透”；“把酒”一作“把菊”；“人比黄花瘦”一作“人似黄花瘦”；“纱厨”今多作“纱橱”。网站从通行本。

lines.zh: 薄雾浓云愁永昼，瑞脑销金兽。
lines.rhythm: 薄雾/浓云/愁永昼，瑞脑/销金兽
lines.py: bó wù nóng yún chóu yǒng zhòu, ruì nǎo xiāo jīn shòu
lines.lit: Thin mist, thick clouds, grieving through the endless day; the camphor incense burns away in the golden beast.
lines.en: Thin mist and heavy cloud — a long, sad day. In the bronze beast the incense slowly burns away.

lines.zh: 佳节又重阳，玉枕纱厨，半夜凉初透。
lines.rhythm: 佳节/又重阳，玉枕/纱厨，半夜/凉初透
lines.py: jiā jié yòu chóng yáng, yù zhěn shā chú, bàn yè liáng chū tòu
lines.lit: The fine festival, Double Ninth again; jade pillow, gauze bed-curtain — at midnight the cold first seeps through.
lines.en: Double Ninth has come round again. On my jade pillow, behind gauze curtains, the midnight chill begins to creep in.

lines.zh: 东篱把酒黄昏后，有暗香盈袖。
lines.rhythm: 东篱/把酒/黄昏后，有暗香/盈袖
lines.py: dōng lí bǎ jiǔ huáng hūn hòu, yǒu àn xiāng yíng xiù
lines.lit: By the eastern hedge, holding wine after dusk; there is a faint fragrance filling my sleeves.
lines.en: At dusk I drink by the eastern hedge, and a faint scent of flowers fills my sleeves.

lines.zh: 莫道不销魂，帘卷西风，人比黄花瘦。
lines.rhythm: 莫道/不销魂，帘卷/西风，人比/黄花瘦
lines.py: mò dào bù xiāo hún, lián juǎn xī fēng, rén bǐ huáng huā shòu
lines.lit: Don’t say it does not melt the soul: the curtain rolls up in the west wind — the person is thinner than the yellow flowers.
lines.en: Don’t tell me this doesn’t break a heart. When the west wind lifts the curtain, the woman inside is thinner than the chrysanthemums.

words.note: 永：长；昼：白天。现代汉语“昼夜”“白昼”。
一种名贵的香料，又叫龙脑。

words.en: a bronze incense burner shaped like a beast
words.note: 古代的香炉常做成狮子、麒麟等兽形。

words.en: Double Ninth Festival (9th day of the 9th lunar month)
words.note: 今天仍是传统节日，又叫“老人节”，有登高、赏菊的习俗。

words.en: a bed enclosed by gauze curtains
words.note: 古代防蚊的纱帐，今天说“蚊帐”。
出自陶渊明“采菊东篱下”，后来成了菊园的代称。

words.en: to hold a wine cup; to drink
words.note: 把：拿着。现代汉语“把握”“把手”。
现代汉语“充盈”“热泪盈眶”。
莫：不要；道：说。现代汉语“说”。
古义指极度伤心；今天“销魂”多指极其快乐、陶醉，意思变了。
古诗里多指菊花；现代汉语“黄花菜”是另一种植物。

imagery.name: 菊
imagery.zh: 重阳赏菊本是团聚的乐事，她却独自对花；最后又用细瘦的菊花来比自己的憔悴。
imagery.en: Chrysanthemums belong to a family festival, yet she faces them alone — and in the end the slender flowers become a mirror of her own thinness.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 黄昏独自饮酒，想借酒消愁，愁却更深。
imagery.en: She drinks alone at dusk to ease the longing, and it only grows.

imagery.name: 秋风
imagery.zh: 西风卷起帘子，带来秋凉，也把憔悴的人“露”了出来。
imagery.en: The west wind lifts the curtain, bringing autumn’s chill and revealing the worn-out woman inside.
